motivation: Rewrite five genuinely compounded legacy core mock prompts so each is a short recall or ordered fill-in-the-gaps question; preserve old valid model answers and user progress IDs.

revisions.subject: Physics
revisions.originalFront: What common forces might appear on a free-body diagram?
revisions.originalBack: Weight acts vertically down; normal contact force acts perpendicular to a surface; tension acts along a string; drag/friction acts opposite relative motion or its tendency.
revisions.newFront: Fill: weight acts ___; normal acts ___; tension acts ___; friction acts ___.
revisions.newBack: vertically down; perpendicular to surface; along string; opposes relative motion
accept: downwards; perpendicular; along the rope; opposes relative sliding
down; normal to surface; along the string; opposes slipping
reject: weight up; normal vertical; tension sideways; friction always downhill
down; parallel to surface; perpendicular to string; along slipping direction
down; perpendicular; along rope; opposite direction of motion

revisions.subject: Physics
revisions.originalFront: What is a couple, and what is the moment of a couple?
revisions.originalBack: Two equal, opposite, parallel forces with separated lines of action. Resultant force = 0. Moment of the couple = Fd, where d is the perpendicular separation.
revisions.newFront: What is a couple of forces?
revisions.newBack: Two equal, opposite, parallel forces acting along different lines of action.
accept: Two equal opposite parallel forces with separated lines of action.
An equal and opposite pair of parallel forces, offset from each other.
reject: Two equal and opposite forces acting along the same line.
Two unbalanced forces producing a net force instead of a pure turning effect.

revisions.subject: Physics
revisions.originalFront: State Newton's third law and explain why the two forces do not cancel.
revisions.originalBack: Interacting objects exert equal, opposite forces of the same type on each other, acting on different objects, so they do not cancel on one object.
revisions.newFront: Why don't Newton's third-law forces cancel on one object?
revisions.newBack: They act on different interacting objects, not on the same object.
accept: The action and reaction forces act on separate bodies.
Each third-law force is exerted on a different object.
reject: They act on the same object and therefore cancel.
Newton's third-law pair always add to give a larger force on one body.

revisions.subject: Physics
revisions.originalFront: Velocity changes from −8 to −2 m s⁻¹ in 3.0 s. Find acceleration and describe the speed.
revisions.originalBack: a = (−2 − (−8))/3 = +2.0 m s⁻². Speed falls from 8 to 2 m s⁻¹.
revisions.newFront: Velocity changes from −8 to −2 m s⁻¹ in 3.0 s. Find acceleration.

revisions.subject: Chemistry
revisions.originalFront: What catalyst is associated with catalytic cracking and what products are valuable?
revisions.originalBack: A zeolite catalyst; valuable products include motor fuels and aromatic hydrocarbons.
revisions.newFront: Which catalyst is used for catalytic cracking?
accept: A zeolite, an acidic aluminosilicate catalyst.
reject: Concentrated sulfuric acid is the catalytic cracking catalyst.
Platinum is the standard zeolite cracking catalyst.
